name: Trading Capacity 4 Code
definition: Specifies the role of a trading party in a transaction.

RISP.name: Riskless Principal
RISP.definition: Trading as a riskless principal, ie, the order to buy(sell) has been simultaneously offset by an order to sell (buy) with another party.

PROP.name: Proprietary
PROP.definition: Trading for its firm. The transaction affects the firm's own account, not that of its customers.

AGEN.name: Agent
AGEN.definition: Trading as Agent on behalf of a customer.

OAGN.name: Other Agent
OAGN.definition: Acting as an agent for a party other than a customer.

PRAG.name: Principal Agent
PRAG.definition: Acting as an agent for some executions and principal for others in the same transaction.

BAGN.name: Acting Agent
BAGN.definition: Party acting as an agent for both customer and another person.

INFI.name: Investment Firm
INFI.definition: Any legal person whose regular occupation or business is the provision of one or more investment services to third parties and/or the performance of one or more investment activities on a professional basis.

MKTM.name: Market Maker
MKTM.definition: Dealer or specialist that is trading for their own account in the OTC market. Market makers are expected to maintain an orderly market by being available to buy or sell.

MLTF.name: Multilateral Trading Facility
MLTF.definition: Multilateral Trading Facility (MTF) is a multilateral system which brings together multiple third-party buying and selling interests in financial instruments in a way that results in a contract.

RMKT.name: Regulated Market
RMKT.definition: Regulated market on which financial instruments can be traded according to rules defined by the stock exchange.

SINT.name: Systematic Internaliser
SINT.definition: Firms which, on an organised, frequent and systematic basis, deal on their own account by executing client orders outside a regulated market or an MTF. SIs have the obligation to provide, and make public, a definite bid and offer quote for liquid securities.

TAGT.name: Transfer Agent
TAGT.definition: Party appointed by the Fund Management Company. It updates records of investor accounts to reflect the daily investor purchases, redemptions, switches, transfers, and re-registrations. It ensures the timely settlement of transactions, and may provide tax information to the investor and/or to its intermediaries. It may calculate, collect, and rebate commissions. It prepares and distributes confirmations reflecting transactions, resulting in unit or cash account movements to the investor or the investor's intermediary. It responds to inquiries concerning account status, and processes the income distribution.
